thread:
mira: Heads up — we've been seeing intermittent packet drops and elevated temperatures on the backbone bridge switches feeding racks in eu-central-1 since 22:00 UTC. GPU throughput for pool-gpu-eu2 dropped ~15%. Planning a phased reboot + switch firmware patch Tues 00:30-03:30 UTC. Need capacity/backfill plan and comms.
ops-bot: [ALERT] switch: backbone-eu-bridge-3 temp spike 87C -> hardware warnings. Link flaps 3x in 10m. Ticket #INC-1891 created.
sanjay: Thanks Mira. Can we avoid full rack drains? Suggest 3-phase approach: 1) patch leaf switches + quick reboot, 2) move live jobs off 10% of GPU capacity into canary pools, 3) reboot affected racks. That keeps latency SLOs.
noah: Agree with phased. We should map tenant affinity to racks first. Pool mapping shows pool-gpu-eu2 spans racks r12-r20, with r14 & r17 carrying heavy RL jobs. We should drain r17 first and divert to dedicated-burst-1.
lena: Quick capacity numbers: today peak reserved usage 78% on eu2. Dedicated-burst-1 has ~12% free but cold-starts can add ~6% more after warmup. If we offload, cost estimate for 3h bump ~ $2.3k. Are we okay with that?
tess: We need customer comms. Can we keep an option for a shorter window (45m per phase) if telemetry looks good? Also need to escalate for any infra customers with pinned nodes.
infra-oncall: Proposed runbook: phase A (00:30-01:15): warm up burst pool + cordon r17, migrate pods with `bin/migrate-tenants --from=r17 --to=burst1 --max-parallel=20`.
noah: Migration command we used last week worked well. Include KV cache warmup step: `curl -X POST https://ops.internal/cache/warm?pool=burst1` before traffic switch.
sanjay: Also add preflight checks: `./scripts/check-pool-capacity --region eu-central --pools pool-gpu-eu2,burst1` and sample output parsing.
ops-bot: [RUNBOOK] preflight-checks passed on pools: pool-gpu-eu2(78% used), burst1(12% free) — recommend proceed with canary drain.
mira: Good. For rollback: if packet loss >1% or GPU tail latency >500ms for 5m, abort and re-route traffic to us-west fallback. Add an automated fallback policy: `route-policy set --region eu-central --fallback us-west1 --threshold 1%packet_loss`.
lena: Noted on costs — finance ok with $2.3k one-off, but asks to minimize burst. Consider compressing phases to 40m if telemetry is green and using KV cache to reduce migration time.
tess: I'll draft a short customer-facing blurb: "Planned maintenance in eu-central: small, phased reboots to update network firmware. Some jobs may be briefly paused while we migrate capacity. Expected impact: short performance fluctuation for 5-10m per phase. We'll monitor and rollback if needed." Share before EOD.
mira: Scheduling: Tue 00:30 UTC start, teams oncall: infra-oncall, sanjay (network lead), noah (scheduler lead). Will post an incident channel update 30m before and a follow-up status after each phase. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: [SCHEDULE] maintenance window created: 2026-03-23 00:30-03:30 UTC. Link: https://ops.internal/maint/8543219999
noah: I'll pre-stage kube drain hooks and a smaller canary (r12) at 23:45 UTC to validate scripts.
sanjay: One more: ensure BGP adjacencies are stable post-switch reboot. We'll run `bgp-check --peer spine1` after each phase. If adj down, hold sequence and engage network hardware team.
mira: Perfect. I'll sync with comms + post the short blurb. Thanks everyone — we'll run the preflight at 23:15 UTC and reconvene in this thread with the pass/fail.
